Man Arrested on Suspicion of Arson in Spokane Wildfire

facts.text: A man, identified as Aaron F. Farinacci, 37, of Spokane, was arrested and charged with first-degree arson in connection with the Old Trails fire in Spokane, Washington.
The wildfires destroyed hundreds of structures, including homes.
Forecasts indicated that winds would increase on Friday and Saturday, along with dry conditions in parts of central Washington.
The arrest was connected to one of three wildfires burning in the Spokane, Washington, area.
Nearly one quarter of Spokane's residents were displaced by the wildfires.
Spokane County Sheriff John Nowels said Farinacci had a prior manslaughter conviction in Arizona.
According to the Phoenix New Times, the victim in the Arizona case was Farinacci's father, who was shot and killed at their home in Mesa in 2010.
Nowels said Farinacci was expected to make his first court appearance on Tuesday.
Officials said a witness reported seeing Farinacci kneeling near the site where the fire started.
The Old Trails fire began on Saturday north-west of downtown Spokane and crossed the Spokane River.
More than 67,000 people were told to evacuate because of three fires named Old Trail, Autumn Lane and Fairview.
By early Tuesday the three Spokane-area fires had burned about 16 square miles (41 sq km).
At least 15 wildfires were burning across Washington state, covering at least 390 square miles.
Washington state's congressional delegation sent a letter to Donald Trump on Monday urging approval of an expedited emergency declaration.
Governor Bob Ferguson said he spoke with the White House over the weekend after issuing a state emergency declaration.
Cpl Mark Gregory of the Spokane sheriff's office said on Monday that 14 people remained unaccounted for.
More than 1,000 firefighters, many from other states, had arrived by Monday to work on the fires.
A National Weather Service Spokane office bulletin issued Tuesday morning stated that smoke would continue over the region.
Forecasters indicated a return to extremely critical fire weather conditions.
Dozens of wildfires are burning across the western United States.
A "firenado," described as a twister of flames, was recorded on video amid the wildfire conditions.
NBC's Morgan Chesky reported on the wildfires.
TODAY's Al Roker provided the weather forecast in the segment.
The video segment is dated Aug. 4, 2026.
The segment titled "West Coast Wildfires Rage on as Arson Suspect Arrested" has a runtime of 3 minutes and 51 seconds.
Micaela Jaime and her family traveled by boat onto Lake Spokane as wildfires approached.
Primary elections are being held in five states.
NPR reported that Michigan is a focus for Democrats observing how progressive candidates perform in races.

topics.title: Strait of Hormuz talks with Iran

articles.title: Trump claims Iran talks are underway as Tehran denies it
Hormuz Opening Uncertain After New Strike
Trump threatens Iran with "decapitation" as questions surround Strait of Hormuz, deal's future
Talks With Iran to Reopen Strait of Hormuz Make Progress, Officials Say
Stocks in Record Territory as Investors Shake Off Worries
Progress made in Strait of Hormuz talks, Rubio says

facts.text: A cargo vessel was struck by an unknown projectile off Oman's coast near the Strait of Hormuz on Monday night, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre.

Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed bin Mohammed Al Ansari said mediators in Qatar, Pakistan and Oman are working together, coordinating with Oman to exchange ideas and drafts between the two sides and seeking to create conditions for a resumption of direct U.S.-Iran dialogue.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC that the United States could reach a deal with Iran to open the Strait of Hormuz within a day or two, by Wednesday.
Trump threatened Iran, saying he wanted to give Iran "every last chance before decapitation."
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday that progress had been made in talks over reopening the Strait of Hormuz but that nothing had been finalized, and he expressed optimism.

President Trump said negotiations with Iran were taking place, with a first phase concerning the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz — possibly as early as Tuesday — and a second phase addressing Iran's nuclear program.
Trump wrote on Truth Social that Iran was "unbelievably duplicitous," saying Iran requested talks and then said no discussions were being held.
Iranian Foreign Affairs Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei told reporters that Iran does not currently have negotiations with the United States.
Baghaei said Iran is in discussions with Oman over a temporary safe route through the Strait of Hormuz and has no plans to host foreign delegations or send negotiators abroad in the coming days.
Maritime sources told Reuters that the vessel struck near the Strait of Hormuz was a dry bulk ship, that its crew abandoned the vessel, and that one seafarer was missing.
Talks concerning the opening of the Strait of Hormuz were ongoing at the time of the ship strike, and the reopening of the strait remained uncertain following it.
Brent crude rose by 2.7% on Tuesday.
Oil prices declined sharply amid expectations regarding talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
Stock prices were in record territory as investors shook off worries.
About five minutes into trading on Tuesday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 1.3% at 53,832.40, the S&P 500 rose 0.6% to 7,644.30, and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 1.1% to 26,185.99.
Qatar said draft language of an agreement was being circulated.
Trump had earlier called off new strikes on Iran.
An NBC News analysis of MarineTraffic data found that at least six vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, compared with about 100 ships per day in peacetime.
Questions remain about a possible deal concerning the Strait of Hormuz.
CBS News correspondent Imtiaz Tyab presented the report on the situation.
Rubio said the United States is involved in the talks between Oman and Iran.
Rubio said the denuclearization of Iran is the "ultimate deal" and that the immediate focus is on the straits.
Yemen's Houthis said on Tuesday that they conducted a drone strike on a target at an airport in southern Saudi Arabia, and Saudi authorities did not comment on the claim.

The Indian vessel MSV Faize Noore Oliya sank on Tuesday after being struck by a projectile near Yemeni waters; 14 people aboard, including 13 Indians, were rescued by the Yemeni Coast Guard and taken to the Port of Mokha.
The Labor Department reported on Tuesday that U.S. employers posted 7.36 million job vacancies in June, down from 7.54 million in May.
Kpler data released Tuesday showed about 30 million barrels of Iraqi crude oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz between July 4 and Aug. 4.
Iraqi oil minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair said last month that Iraq's crude export revenues barely exceed $1.5 billion per month, compared with up to $8 billion previously.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Tuesday that Iran would defend its borders and interests but was not seeking to expand the war.

facts.text: Michigan holds primary contests for a U.S. Senate seat and for governor.
Rep. Wesley Bell faces Cori Bush in a rematch primary in St. Louis, Missouri's 1st Congressional District.
Five states hold primary elections on Tuesday.
Wesley Bell holds a seat in the U.S. House of Representatives.
The U.S.-Israel relationship is a subject of attention in the Bell-Bush contest.
Bell and Bush have previously competed against each other in an election.
Democratic primary elections have taken place in Michigan, Wisconsin and Minnesota.
The Midwest primaries serve as a test of whether progressive candidates can win in competitive states.
The progressive movement is divided between Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Rep. Ro Khanna over who will succeed Bernie Sanders as its leader.
Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Ro Khanna are members of the U.S. House of Representatives.
Michigan's Senate primary is described as the most expensive Democratic Senate primary race to date.
The NBC News report is dated August 4, 2026.
The primaries take place ahead of the November midterm elections.
NBC's Shaquille Brewster reported on the primary races.
Steve Kornacki appeared on TODAY to provide analysis of the primary races.
The video segment titled "Democrats Face Big Test in Critical Michigan Primary" has a runtime of 5 minutes and 8 seconds.
Marie Gluesenkamp Perez is a two-term Democratic congresswoman representing Washington state's third district.
Washington's third district primary is scheduled for Tuesday, with the top two finishers advancing to the November general election regardless of party.
Nine candidates appear on the primary ballot in Washington's third district, including Democrat Brent Hennrich and Republican state senator John Braun.
Republican Jaime Herrera Beutler won Washington's third district in 2010 and held the seat for six terms.
Gluesenkamp Perez defeated Trump-endorsed Joe Kent in the 2022 election for Washington's third district.
Donald Trump won Washington's third district in all three of his presidential campaigns, most recently by approximately three points.
In 2024, Gluesenkamp Perez received roughly seven points more support in the district than the Democratic presidential nominee.
Gluesenkamp Perez owns an auto repair shop.
Brent Hennrich ran for Washington's third district seat in 2022 before withdrawing, and said he stepped out of the race to unify Democrats.

LaDonna Kirkpatrick, chair of the 18th Legislative District Democrats, cited Gluesenkamp Perez's votes for the Save Act, a bill restricting how public schools address gender identity, and federal funding tied to the war in Iran.
Thea Zahn, chair of the 20th legislative district Democrats, said she would not vote for Gluesenkamp Perez.
Terri Niles, chair of the 17th Legislative District Democrats, said the district is Republican and that flipping the House is the goal for Democrats.
An Emerson College poll conducted in mid-July for the Northwest Progressive Institute found Gluesenkamp Perez and Braun tied.
John Braun is the Republican leader in the Washington state senate and received Donald Trump's endorsement in April and backing from the National Republican Congressional Committee.

facts.text: Russian officials said a Ukrainian drone strike hit a beach on the Black Sea, killing people.
Russian officials said seven people, including three children, were killed in the explosion in Gelendzhik on Monday.

Russia described the incident as a deliberate attack on civilians, and Krasnodar region governor Veniamin Kondratyev said on Telegram it was a deliberate strike by the Kyiv government against the civilian population.
Russia said about 40 people were injured in the incident.
Russian officials said 58 people were injured in the explosion.
The report is dated Aug. 4, 2026.
NBC News verified video of the explosion in Gelendzhik that was shared on social media.
Moscow carried out aerial strikes on Ukraine following the explosion.
Ukrainian officials neither confirmed nor denied responsibility for the explosion in Gelendzhik.
Andriy Kovalenko, head of the Ukrainian National Security and Defense Council's Centre for Countering Disinformation, said Russian air defenses shot down a drone onto people on the beach.
Kovalenko said in a statement that Vladimir Putin was responsible for the deaths of the Russians killed in the explosion.
Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova said on Friday that at least 61 people were killed and more than 320 wounded in Ukrainian shelling and drone strikes between July 24 and July 31.
Aleksandr Drozdenko, governor of the Leningrad region, said early Tuesday that an attack hit a warehouse in the region.
Ukrainian officials said Russian missile, drone and bomb attacks killed at least 377 people in July, the highest monthly total since April 2022.
The Sumy regional administration said early Tuesday that two children and an elderly woman were killed in overnight strikes.
Zaporizhzhia regional chief Ivan Fedorov said Tuesday that two people were killed in the region, and had said a day earlier that one person was killed when Russia dropped eight glide bombs.
Turkey called on Russia and Ukraine on Tuesday to improve navigational safety after a Turkish-owned vessel was struck and people onboard were injured.
Vladimir Putin launched a large-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Ukraine and Russia continue to exchange strikes.
CBS News correspondent Aidan Stretch reported on the incident.
NBC News published video items on Ukrainian strikes on Russian tankers in the Sea of Azov and Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow.

topics.title: Eaton Fire cause attributed to Southern California Edison equipment

articles.title: Eaton Fire in Altadena sparked by SoCal Edison electric tower, probe finds
Southern California Edison equipment blamed for 2025 Eaton Fire in Los Angeles

facts.text: Los Angeles County Fire officials released on Tuesday the conclusion of an 18-month investigation into the origin of the Eaton Fire, attributing it to Southern California Edison equipment.
The report determined that electrical arcing on an out-of-service Southern California Edison transmission tower caused the Eaton Fire.
The Eaton Fire began on January 7, 2025.
The Eaton Fire destroyed or damaged more than 9,000 homes and businesses, primarily in Altadena, and also affected Pasadena.
Nineteen people died in the Eaton Fire, according to the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner.
The investigation was conducted jointly by the Los Angeles County Fire Department's Arson Fire Investigation Unit and Cal Fire.
The investigation involved retained electrical and metallurgical experts.
The report stated that arcing events ejected hot metal particles that fell onto dry vegetation below the towers.
The transmission tower is located on a ridge above the Eaton Wash.
Another blaze began the same day as the Eaton Fire.
Firefighters took nearly a month to extinguish the Eaton Fire.
The Eaton Fire burned 22 square miles (57 square kilometers).
CBS LA contacted Southern California Edison for comment and did not immediately receive a response.
Southern California Edison announced last month that it had paid more than $314 million to fire victims through its Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program.
Southern California Edison claimed in lawsuits earlier in 2025 that Los Angeles County agencies did not send timely evacuation warnings to residents in east and west Altadena.
Eighteen of the 19 people who died in the Eaton Fire lived in west Altadena.
Southern California Edison claimed that water agencies, including Pasadena Water and Power, did not supply enough water as the fire spread.
Los Angeles County declined to comment on the court filings.
The Palisades Fire killed 12 people and destroyed more than 6,800 homes and buildings in Pacific Palisades.

articles.title: Jeanine Pirro Faces Uncertain Future After Reflecting Pool Case
Pirro meets with Trump at White House amid questions about her future

facts.text: U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro dropped charges against a former Olympic canoeist, David Hearn, who had been indicted in connection with damage to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.
President Donald Trump criticized Pirro's decision to drop the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool charges.
NBC News describes Jeanine Pirro as a long-time ally of President Donald Trump.
NBC's Gabe Gutierrez reported on the Jeanine Pirro story for TODAY.
The NBC News video segment about Jeanine Pirro is dated Aug. 4, 2026, and runs 1 minute and 53 seconds.
Sources familiar with the matter told ABC News that Pirro met with Trump at the White House on Monday afternoon.
Trump said Pirro "choked" and "folded like an umbrella" in dropping the Reflecting Pool charges.
The White House did not respond to a request for comment about the meeting between Trump and Pirro.
A White House official directed ABC News to Trump's earlier Oval Office comments when asked about the future of Pirro's job.
Trump said during an Oval Office event on Monday that he was "very disappointed" in Pirro's decision to dismiss the felony indictment against canoeist David Hearn.
Pirro dismissed the felony indictment against David Hearn on Friday.
Pirro stated in a 20-page filing that the damage to the Reflecting Pool was caused by flawed installation by the contractor rather than vandalism.
Hearn was arrested at the Reflecting Pool in late June and charged with a felony for allegedly causing more than $1,000 in damage.
Hearn pleaded not guilty and said he had only touched a piece of the liner that was peeled from the bottom.
Pirro cited internal National Park Service communication from June 11 that raised concerns about the peeling pool liner.
Pirro dropped misdemeanor cases against three other people related to destruction of property at the Reflecting Pool.
Trump wrote in a social media post on Saturday that he did not know what Pirro was thinking and that the incident was a case of vandalism.
Pirro said in her Friday court filing that she visited the pool on July 1.
The Reflecting Pool was drained for repairs shortly after the Fourth of July holiday and is currently empty and fenced off from the public.
Trump said on Monday that the Reflecting Pool would be fixed and reopened within two weeks at most.
